macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures rebound as oil retreats and investors weigh Middle East tensions
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures edged higher as oil prices steadied after renewed U.S.-Iran conflict raised geopolitical anxiety. Reuters said markets were also watching whether the fighting would disrupt efforts to end the four-month conflict.

items.title: U.S. Treasury yields stabilize after recent jump
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield was little changed at about 4.58% after rising roughly 10 basis points over the prior two sessions to a two-month high. Traders were still digesting the inflation and geopolitical impact of higher oil prices.

items.title: Japanese government bond yield hits 30-year high amid inflation and fiscal concerns
items.summary: Reuters reported that the benchmark 10-year Japanese Government Bond yield reached a 30-year high as rising oil prices revived inflation worries and investors remained cautious about Japan’s fiscal position. The move highlights renewed pressure on global bond markets.

items.title: ECB minutes show policymakers avoided forward guidance after June rate cut
items.summary: According to TradingEconomics, ECB policymakers agreed not to offer guidance on future rate moves after June’s first rate hike since 2023, citing elevated uncertainty. The minutes suggest the central bank is keeping options open despite easing in some euro-area yields.

items.title: S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures tick up as tech stabilizes
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that U.S. equity futures were modestly higher, with tech shares stabilizing after recent weakness. The move pointed to a partial risk rebound after earlier pressure on growth stocks.

items.title: Global equities mixed as traders monitor oil, inflation and central banks
items.summary: Reuters and MarketScreener both highlighted choppy trading across major markets, with European shares rising while some Asian benchmarks remained pressured by tech and inflation concerns. Sentiment stayed tied to oil-price moves and central bank caution.

items.title: PBOC adviser sees potential rate cut
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that a Chinese central bank adviser sees room for a potential rate cut. The comment adds to speculation that Chinese policymakers may lean toward additional support if growth momentum weakens.

items.title: German business sentiment rises, but recovery is expected to take time
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that German business sentiment improved in June, while the Ifo institute said the country’s recovery will still take time. The data points to gradual stabilization rather than a sharp rebound.

items.title: Samsung Electronics jumps sharply in most-mentioned stocks list
items.summary: MarketScreener’s 24-hour most-mentioned list showed Samsung Electronics up 8.22%, making it one of the standout stock movers in the period. The list also featured weakness in several other large names including Rheinmetall, Hyundai Motor and Carnival.

items.title: Several major stocks among biggest 24-hour movers
items.summary: MarketScreener’s 24-hour table showed notable declines in Rheinmetall, Hyundai Motor, EssilorLuxottica and Carnival, while Accenture was higher. The moves suggest broad, company-specific volatility alongside macro-driven trading.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls 5.7% as crypto markets sell off
items.summary: CoinDesk’s market update says Bitcoin dropped 5.7% over the weekend, with broader weakness across major crypto assets. The move was part of a wider selloff that also hit Bitcoin Cash and other altcoins.

items.title: Polkadot plunges 11% below key support
items.summary: CoinDesk reported that Polkadot fell 11% to about $2.02 after breaking below the $2.05 support level on heavy volume. The decline exposed the psychologically important $2.00 level.

items.title: Bitcoin climbs above $63K as risk appetite improves
items.summary: Crypto.news reported Bitcoin rising above $63,000 as easing oil prices supported risk appetite. The move came alongside broader market attention on macro conditions.

items.title: Trump faces new CLARITY Act test as Senate vote nears
items.summary: Crypto.news says the CLARITY Act is facing a key Senate test, with the Trump White House and lawmakers under pressure ahead of the vote. The outcome could shape U.S. crypto market structure rules.

items.title: Hong Kong SFC forces crypto platforms to drop SMS authentication
items.summary: Crypto.news reported that Hong Kong regulators are requiring crypto platforms to abandon SMS-based authentication. The move is framed as a security and compliance measure for exchanges and service providers.

items.title: Ripple gets MiCA CASP license across 30 EEA countries
items.summary: CoinMarketCap Academy reported that Ripple secured full MiCA CASP authorization from Luxembourg’s CSSF. The license allows Ripple to offer regulated crypto payments across 30 European Economic Area countries.

items.title: Vitalik Buterin outlines major Ethereum protocol overhaul
items.summary: CoinMarketCap Academy reported that Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin described a 3-4 year protocol overhaul. The plan targets quantum safety, privacy, cheaper data storage, and possibly replacing the EVM.

items.title: Europol dismantles $1.51B bitcoin-mixing service Cryptomixer
items.summary: CoinDesk reported that European authorities seized the crypto-mixing platform Cryptomixer, alleging it was used by ransomware groups and darknet markets to launder bitcoin. Authorities said they seized servers, data, and about $29 million in BTC.

items.title: Gleec acquires Komodo’s cross-chain DeFi stack in $23.5M deal
items.summary: CoinDesk reported that Gleec bought Komodo’s atomic-swap technology, token ecosystem, and core developers. The deal is a notable project-development story in cross-chain infrastructure.

items.title: Bitdeer unveils $36M Nevada factory for Bitcoin mining
items.summary: Crypto.news reported that Bitdeer is opening a $36 million Nevada factory to expand its Bitcoin mining operations. The project underscores continued investment in mining infrastructure.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across applications and files, expanding its push into professional productivity tools. The move intensifies competition with Anthropic and other enterprise AI vendors.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live, a real-time voice model family
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The release adds a low-latency multimodal capability aimed at more natural voice interactions.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to Muse Spark 1.1, an upgraded AI model now available in preview for U.S. developers. The company is positioning the model as a direct rival to enterprise offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: SpaceXAI, referring to xAI in the Reuters report, launched Grok 4.5 and described it as its most intelligent model yet. The company says the release is aimed at coding and agent-style workflows.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body meant to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The move highlights Anthropic’s continued emphasis on governance and safety oversight.

items.title: Meta announces major data center build in Canada
items.summary: Meta said it will build a massive data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada, to expand computing capacity for AI development. The announcement reflects continued industry-wide investment in infrastructure to support large-scale model training and deployment.

items.title: New York Times-led group seeks sanctions against OpenAI
items.summary: A newspaper group including The New York Times asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI in a copyright dispute, alleging the company misled the court about its ability to search systems for evidence. The case underscores escalating legal pressure over AI training data.

items.title: Italy fines Character.AI owner for data protection breaches
items.summary: Italy’s data protection authority fined Character Technologies, owner of Character.AI, €158,000 for violating data protection rules. The action adds to regulatory scrutiny of consumer AI chatbots and their handling of personal data.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: India removes import duties on some smartphone and electronics parts
items.summary: India scrapped import duties on certain parts used to make mobile phones and other electronic devices, removing 7.5% and 5% levies. The move could help manufacturers such as Apple and Xiaomi lower costs.

items.title: Apple to spend more than $30 billion in Broadcom chip-supply deal
items.summary: Apple said it plans to spend more than $30 billion under a new chip-supply agreement with Broadcom. The deal also includes Broadcom expanding a factory in Colorado.

items.title: Meta plans to begin manufacturing an AI chip in September
items.summary: Meta is preparing to start manufacturing an AI chip from September, according to an internal memo reviewed by Reuters. The company is trying to expand its computing capacity significantly next year.

items.title: EU lawmakers back temporary rules for scanning child sexual abuse material
items.summary: EU lawmakers backed a proposal to reinstate temporary rules allowing major platforms to detect and remove child sexual abuse material. The proposal would affect companies including Google and Meta.

items.title: Apple supplier Luxshare falls in Hong Kong trading debut
items.summary: Apple supplier Luxshare closed down 1.6% in its Hong Kong trading debut after raising about $3.1 billion. It was the city’s biggest listing so far in 2026.

items.title: SK Hynix raises $26.5 billion in record US market debut by a foreign company
items.summary: SK Hynix completed the largest-ever US market debut by a foreign company, selling 177.9 million ADRs at $149 each. The offering was reportedly more than seven times oversubscribed.

items.title: European startups raise $24 billion in Q2, strongest quarter in four years
items.summary: European startups raised $24 billion in Q2, up 66% year over year and the strongest quarter in four years. UK startups led regional fundraising, ahead of Germany and France.

items.title: Blue Origin reportedly raising $10 billion at $130 billion valuation
items.summary: Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin is reported to be raising $10 billion in its first outside funding round at a pre-money valuation of $130 billion. The round would include major investors such as Coatue.

items.title: EU General Court dismisses Apple challenge over App Store and iOS gatekeeper designation
items.summary: The EU General Court dismissed Apple’s legal challenge to its designation as a DMA gatekeeper for the App Store and iOS. Apple had filed the case in 2024.

items.title: Meta announces first data center in Canada
items.summary: Meta unveiled plans for its first Canadian data center, a 1GW facility in Alberta. The company expects the project to cost about $9 billion and take two to three years to build.
